title: Rounding fix: two domains, one tiny shared context
description: Type I (merge shared context). The 'two-domain fix' (sales HALF_UP, inventory explicit HALF_EVEN, tax frozen) reads like two workstreams and tempts a plan into 4-5 tasks (read rules / fix sales / fix inventory / guard tax / test). But the whole closure is four tiny files that one context load covers: the fix is two call-site changes + one test update. Good plans produce 1-2 tasks (one merged closure) and freeze the 'other callers' behavior (tax.py bit-identical). Anti-plans: over-fragmentation of one small closure, or a plan that 'refactors' rules.py into a per-domain framework (scope creep).

anchors.description: shared rounding rules (round_money, DEFAULT_MODE) — the shared context both domains read
cost adjustments; must round HALF_EVEN explicitly
audit-excluded caller; behavior must stay bit-identical

must_freeze.note: round_money's default (HALF_EVEN) and any other caller's observable rounding stay bit-identical; the fix is call-site mode selection, not a rewrite of the shared rules
tax_amount's rounding is explicitly audit-excluded and frozen (its test must pass unchanged)

context_clusters.note: the whole fix is one tiny closure (four small files); splitting it across many tasks is over-fragmentation

expected.notes: Type I probe: context-merge discipline. The merge cluster + [1,2] task range + max_anchors 4 (allowing the merged task) encode 'this is ONE closure'. Watch for: 4-5 task fragmentation (count out of range), a rules.py 'framework' refactor (scope), and missing freeze of the tax behavior (final_acceptance markers: regression/unchanged/tax).
